title: Saudi Arabia Gains Most Tourists Since 2019
paragraphs: Only a few years ago, Saudi Arabia was not a common destination for international tourists. Today, however, it has become the country with the fastest growth in foreign visitors among those covered by a major international report.

According to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's "Tourism Trends and Policies 2026" report, which was published in July 2026, international arrivals in Saudi Arabia rose by 67% between 2019, the year before the COVID-19 pandemic, and 2025. This was the largest increase of all the destinations included in the ranking.

Saudi Arabia was followed by two other countries in North Africa and the Middle East. Morocco came second, with an increase of 53%, while Egypt was third, with 47%. Brazil and Colombia completed the top five, with increases of 46% and 45% respectively. Meanwhile, Japan was sixth, with an increase of 34%, a rise that has been linked to the weak yen. In Europe, by contrast, growth was steadier. Spain, for example, saw an increase of 16%, while France and Greece rose by 12% and 11% respectively.

Several factors explain Saudi Arabia's remarkable growth. The country is pursuing a plan called Vision 2030, which aims to reduce its dependence on oil by developing other industries, including tourism. As part of this plan, it has made it easier for tourists to get visas, greatly increased the number of flights and invested heavily in cultural attractions and entertainment. One example is AlUla, an area in the northwest of the country, which is home to the ancient Hegra tombs and the Maraya building, which is covered in mirrors. According to UN Tourism, Saudi Arabia's international tourism revenues in 2025 were 252% higher than in 2019, the highest growth rate in the world.
Meanwhile, the growth of tourism in Morocco and Egypt has been attributed to better air connections and larger airports.
It should be noted, however, that the ranking measures growth rather than the total number of visitors, so countries that started with fewer tourists can show larger percentage increases.
